questions.questionText:
Section Three: Reading Passage II

1. Research suggests that our level of happiness depends partly on factors we cannot control—our genes and our life circumstances. But our level of happiness is also shaped by the choices we make. If you've been chasing wealth, fame, good looks, material things, and power, you may be looking for happiness in all the wrong places. According to psychologists, the following are some of the factors which make people happier.

2. To begin with, people who form close relationships tend to be happier than those do not. The number of friends one has is not as important as what matters is the quality of our relationships. Relationships that bring happiness usually involve the sharing of feelings, mutual respect, acceptance, trust, and empathy. The act of forming intimacy and planning and working for the well-being of others can be a source of happiness. This might involve volunteering for an organization or reaching out to support friends and family on a regular basis.

3. People who include spirituality in their daily life also tend to be happier. Practicing spirituality is a way of recognizing and trying to understand the wonder and beauty of existence, some people do this by being a part of a worship group or practicing some people practice yoga or meditation. Some people go for long walks in nature.

4. In addition, people who think positively by being grateful, mindful, and optimistic are more likely to be happy. Being grateful means being thankful. Being mindful means being open to, focusing on, and enjoying the experiences of the present moment. Being optimistic means being hopeful about the future.

53) As discussed in the passage, spirituality is about
options: how devotion to religion is the source of happiness
how we can lead our life properly.
getting happiness by understanding the beauty of nature.
recognizing and knowing more about the environment in which we live.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 3 explains that practicing spirituality involves recognizing and trying to understand the wonder and beauty of existence, which can include yoga, meditation, worship, or long walks in nature.

 This aligns best with 'getting happiness by understanding the beauty of nature.

questions.questionText: The writer believes that
options: people always look for happiness in the wrong places.
wealth, fame, and power are some of factors that make us happy.
wealth, fame, and power are not necessarily the right sources of happiness.
the sources of happiness do not vary according to individuals.
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 1, the writer mentions that chasing wealth, fame, good looks, material things, and power may lead people to look for happiness in the wrong places.

 This implies that these are not necessarily the right sources of happiness.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT an aspect of thinking positively?
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 4 explains that thinking positively involves being grateful (thankful), mindful (enjoying the present), and optimistic (expecting good in the future). 

Being concerned about your position is not mentioned as part of positive thinking.

questions.questionText: According to the passage:
options: The choice we make party responsible for our level of happiness.
Our genes do not influence our level of happiness.
We have no control over the things that make us happy.
We have control over the things that make us happy.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 1 explains that our level of happiness depends partly on factors we cannot control (genes, life circumstances) and partly on the choices we make.

 This means choices are partly responsible for happiness, but we do not have full control."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT the writer’s purpose in this passage?
options: advise people that they need to form close relationships in order tobe happy.
explain why people should be happy in life.
tell people that they have full control over their happiness.
inform people about the choices they have to make themselveshappy.
questions.explanation:
The passage emphasizes factors affecting happiness and the choices we make but does not claim that people have full control over their happiness, as genes and life circumstances also play a role.

 Therefore, option C is NOT the writer’s purpose.

questions.questionText: The writer of the passage believes that in order to be happy one
options: should have as many friends as possible.
should have deeper understanding of friends feelings.
should be able to make others accept his/her thoughts.
should give priority to the benefits of others.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 states that happiness involves 'planning and working for the well-being of others,' and 'volunteering... or reaching out to support friends and family.'

 This aligns with **'should give priority to the benefits of others' (Option D).

 Option B ('deeper understanding of friends feelings') is too narrow compared to the broader idea of working for the well-being of others.

questions.questionText: The writer of the passage believes that in order to be happy one
options: should have as many friends as possible.
should have deeper understanding of friends feelings.
should be able to make others accept his/her thoughts.
should give priority to the benefits of others.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 emphasizes that happiness comes from quality relationships involving sharing feelings, mutual respect, trust, and empathy.

 This aligns best with 'should have deeper understanding of friends' feelings.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT mentioned as a source of happiness?
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 1 mentions that chasing material things may not bring happiness (indicating it is not a source of true happiness).

 Other options—mutual respect, helping others, and sharing feelings—are explicitly mentioned as contributing to happiness.

questions.questionText: Based on the passage, which one of the following is NOT a way of practicing spirituality?
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 lists ways to practice spirituality: being part of a worship group, meditation, yoga, or enjoying nature. Political leadership is not mentioned as a way of practicing spirituality.

questions.questionText: People who do NOT have close relationships are
options: not concerned about happiness in life.
not as happy as those who have.
care more about happiness in life.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 states that people who form close relationships tend to be happier than those who do not.

 Therefore, people without close relationships are not as happy as those who have them.

questions.questionText: Volunteering is mentioned in the passage as a way of
questions.explanation: "Paragraph 2 mentions that forming intimacy and working for the well-being of others, such as volunteering, can be a source of happiness. Therefore, volunteering is associated with getting happiness by helping others.

Section Two: Reading Passage I

1. Air pollution is an issue which concerns us all alike. One can willingly choose or reject a food, a drink or a life comfort, but unfortunately there is little choice for the air we breathe. All, what is there in the air is inhaled by one and all living in those surroundings.

2. Air pollutants is defined as a substance which is present while normally it is not there or is present in an amount exceeding the normal concentrations. It could either be gaseous or a particulate matter. The most common gaseous pollutants are carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, ozone and oxides of sulphur and nitrogen. The common particulate pollutants are the same substances in organic or inorganic origins. Although we of ten talk of the outdoor air pollution caused by industrial and vehicular exhausts, the indoor air pollution may prove to be as or a more cause of health problems.

3. Recognition of air pollution is relatively recent. It is not uncommon to experience a feeling of suffocation in a closed environment, which is often ascribed to the lack of oxygen. Fortunately, however, the composition of air is remarkably constant all over the world. There is about

But such an increase is usually small and temporary unless the room remains airtight. Exposure to poisonous such as carbon monoxide may occur in a closed room, heated by burning coal inside. This may also prove to be fatal.

5. What is more common in a poorly ventilated home is a vague constellation of symptoms described as the sick building syndromes. It is characterized by a general feeling of malaise, headaches, dizziness and irritation of mucus membranes. It may also be accompanied by nausea, itching, aches, pains and depression.

6. Sick building where a getting commomor in big cities, with small houses, which are generally over-furnishing. Some of the major pollutants where indoor concentrations exceed most of the outdoor include gases such as carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, oxide of nitrogen and organic substances like spores, formaldehydes, hydrocarbon aerosols and allergens.

7. The sources are attributed to a variety of construction materials, insulations, furnishings, adhesives, cosmetics, house dusts, fungi and other indoor products.

8. Obviously, the spectrum of pollution is very wide and our options are limited. Indoor pollution may be handled relatively easily by an individual. Moreover, the good work must start from ones' own house.

43) The fact that the composition of air is constant all over the world is an indicator of how
questions.explanation:
The question refers to the statement in Paragraph 3: 'the composition of air is remarkably constant all over the world.

' The word 'constant' means unchanging, and 'all over the world' indicates consistency across geographical locations.

 This stability and consistency across the globe is best summarized by the phrase 'nature is uniform,' meaning nature is consistent and the same everywhere.

questions.questionText: Air pollutant is said to be present when
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 2, the passage defines an air pollutant as a substance that is present when normally it is not there or is present in an amount exceeding the normal concentration.

 Releasing carbon dioxide increases its concentration beyond normal levels, which fits this definition. Therefore, option A is correct.

questions.questionText: The writer of the passage thinks that
options: we can fully control air pollution.
the scale of pollution is too wide to handle in our present capacity.
our understanding of air pollution is low.
individuals can contribute to handling indoor air pollution
questions.explanation:
Option A states that we can fully control air pollution. 

However, paragraph 8 says, 'the spectrum of pollution is very wide and our options are limited,' which shows that the writer does NOT believe we can fully control air pollution.

 Instead, the writer believes individuals can help manage indoor pollution.

questions.questionText: A feeling of suffocation
options: has nothing to do with pollution
questions.explanation:
In the passage, a feeling of suffocation in a closed environment is associated with polluted or poorly ventilated air.

 It suggests that harmful substances or inadequate air circulation may be present.
 Therefore, it is considered an indication of pollution.

questions.questionText: It is NOT stated in the passage that
options: choosing what we eat or drink can give us life comfort.
we have no role in the air we breathe.
air pollution affects us all in different ways.
we can choose or reject a food, a drink or a life comfort when we have the chance.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 1 states that 'One can willingly choose or reject a food, a drink or a life comfort, but unfortunately there is little choice for the air we breathe.'

 This indicates that we do have a role in choosing food or drink, but not the air. 

It does not say that air pollution affects us all in different ways; rather, it says it affects us all alike. Therefore, the statement 'air pollution affects us all in different ways' is NOT stated in the passage.

questions.questionText: The accumulation of carbon dioxide exhaled from lungs
options: is the same in all places.
could result in series illness and death.
increases in an airtight room and could cause suffocation.
is smaller and temporary in airtight rooms.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 explains that in an airtight room, CO₂ from breathing can build up and cause suffocation. Therefore, option C is correct.

questions.questionText: An appropriate title for the passage could be
options: Causes and effects of air pollution
questions.explanation:
The passage explains what air pollutants are, their sources, and their effects on humans, covering both causes and consequences. 

Therefore, 'Causes and effects of air pollution' is the most suitable title.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT true according to the passage?
options: Our indoor activities contribute to air pollution.
Industrial and vehicular exhausts are the main sources of indoor airpollution.
Indoor pollution relatively less than outdoor pollution.
Human beings cannot manage air pollution.
questions.explanation: The passage states industrial and vehicle exhausts mainly cause outdoor pollution, not indoor. So option B is not true.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is mentioned as a source of indoor pollutants?
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 7 lists sources of indoor pollutants, including construction materials, adhesives, house dust, fungi, and cosmetics.

 Therefore, 'Cosmetics' is mentioned as a source of indoor pollutants.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT characteristic of the sick building syndrome?
options: It is the result of the combined effect of various diseases.
It commonly occurs in homes with little or no ventilation.
It is an indistinct collection of symptoms.
It is becoming more common in big cities with small but over-furnished houses.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 5 defines sick building syndrome as a vague collection of symptoms caused by poor ventilation, not by various diseases.

 Therefore, 'It is the result of the combined effect of various diseases' is NOT a characteristic.

DIRECTIONS: Items 69-76 are incomplete sentences. Each sentence is Choose the alternative that best completes the sentence

1) At the meeting, the Chairman allowed ________ of opinions for participation.
questions.explanation:
The sentence refers to allowing a range or variety of opinions. 

The word 'diversity' best completes the sentence, as it means a variety or range of different things.

questions.questionText: The government ________ a new program which will help to solve the problem of over flooding during the rainy season.
questions.explanation:
The sentence refers to introducing a new program. 

The word 'launched' correctly conveys the meaning of starting or initiating a program.

questions.questionText: My friend took out a ________ from a bank to buy a house, but he cloud not pay it back in time.
questions.explanation: The sentence indicates borrowing money from a bank to buy a house, which is called a 'loan.

questions.questionText: The newly married couple has just gone to Hawassa for their ________.
questions.explanation:
A trip taken by a newly married couple is called a 'honeymoon.'
 Therefore, 'honeymoon' is the correct word to complete the sentence.

questions.questionText: Although we are facing many problems at present, we should not be ________ because I am sure that things will become better in the future.
questions.explanation:
The sentence suggests maintaining a positive attitude despite current problems.

 Being 'pessimistic' means expecting the worst, which fits the context of what we should not be.

questions.questionText: The leader of the party will soon ________ that his party has won the recent national election.
questions.explanation:
The sentence refers to publicly announcing the party's victory.

 The word 'declare' correctly conveys this meaning

questions.questionText: The scene of the plane crash where all the passengers on board the plane lost their lives was really ________.
questions.explanation:
The sentence describes a tragic plane crash with total loss of life. 

The word 'terrifying' best expresses the fear and shock associated with the scene.

questions.questionText: I do not need to ________ the mobile numbers of my contacts because I have them all on my mobile phone.
questions.explanation:
The sentence refers to remembering mobile numbers. 

The word 'memorise' correctly completes the sentence.

questions.questionText: The police are still looking for the **murderer** who fatally shot three people and disappeared.
questions.explanation:
The word 'murderer' refers to someone who has unlawfully killed another person.

 Among the options, 'killer' is the closest synonym.

questions.questionText: His job is to **guide** invited guests to their seats in the hall.
questions.explanation:
The word 'guide' in this context means to direct or show the way.

 None of the options exactly match this meaning; however, 'responsibility' comes closest because guiding guests is part of one's duty or role.

questions.questionText: The patient who was in an accident remained **immobile** on the stretcher for about two hours.
questions.explanation:
The word 'immobile' means unable to move. 

Among the options, 'motionless' is the best substitute.

questions.questionText: 6 A father, a mother and children who live together **make up** a family.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'make up' in this context means 'to form' or 'constitute.'

 Among the options, 'form' is the best substitute.

questions.questionText: They wasted some time at the beginning and now they are **under pressure** to complete the work in the time given.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'under pressure' means experiencing stress or anxiety due to the need to perform a task quickly or to a high standard. 

The best synonym for this state is 'tension' (Option A).

 'Struggle' implies difficulty in the task itself, while 'tension' relates to the emotional state of facing the deadline.

questions.questionText: The man says that he can beat anybody in a fight, but actually he is a **cowardly** bully.
questions.explanation:
The word 'cowardly' means lacking courage or being timid. 

Among the options, 'timid' is the closest in meaning

questions.questionText: 70) The police should **heighten** the awareness of the community in order to put the rising criminal acts under control.
questions.explanation: The word 'heighten' means to increase or make greater. Among the options, 'raise' is the best substitute.

questions.questionText:
Directions: Items 1-38 are incomplete sentences. Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.

 Take your umbrella with you. It ________ rain in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: The speaker advises taking an umbrella because there is a possibility of rain. The modal verb 'might' is used to express possibility or a weak probability, which fits the context of preparing for uncertain weather.

questions.questionText: I think I saw you coming out of the Director's office. ________ did you got there?
questions.explanation:
The sentence is asking for a reason. The correct question word used to ask about reason is 'Why'. 

The other options (Who, What, For how) do not correctly fit the context of asking for a reason.

questions.questionText: I eat nearly all kinds of food. ________ drinks, I only like soft drinks and fruit juices.
questions.explanation:
As far as is used to limit or specify a particular topic. In the sentence, the speaker is narrowing the discussion specifically to drinks.

 Therefore, \"As far as drinks\" correctly expresses this limitation. The other options do not fit grammatically or contextually.

questions.questionText:
Bekalu: How ________ do you watch television?

 Dinku: Every evening.
questions.explanation:
The question is asking about frequency. 
The correct question form is How often do you watch television? because often is used to ask about how frequently something happens.

 The other options do not fit grammatically in this context.

questions.questionText: He ________ something at the roadside and started running as fast as he could.
questions.explanation:
The second part of the sentence, 'and started running,' is in the simple past tense. For a sequence of past actions, the preceding action must also be in the simple past tense. 

Therefore, the correct verb is 'saw,' which is the simple past form of 'see'.

questions.questionText: You say your friend has not been around for some time. ________ did you last see him?
questions.explanation:
The question is asking for the specific point in time that the person last saw their friend.

 The question word used to ask about time is 'When.'

questions.questionText: We didn't like the talk show, ________ we switched to the movie channel.
questions.explanation:
The first clause ('We didn't like the talk show') is the cause (reason), and the second clause ('we switched to the movie channel') is the result. 

The conjunction 'so' is used to introduce the result or consequence of the first action or situation. The structure is: Cause, so Result.

questions.questionText: My friend is sometimes hard to convince, but I like him ________.
questions.explanation:
The sentence expresses a contrast between the friend's characteristic ('hard to convince') and the speaker's feeling ('I like him').

 The word 'nonetheless' is an adverb that means 'in spite of that' or 'however,' and is used to show a contrast that is surprising or unexpected. 
It fits the meaning established by the conjunction 'but' at the start of the second clause.

questions.questionText: Tomorrow, Sofanit ________ her assignments the whole day.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'Tomorrow... the whole day' indicates an action that will be in progress over a period of time in the future.

 This requires the Future Continuous Tense, which is formed with 'will be' + the present participle (verb + -ing).
 Therefore, 'will be doing' is the correct form.

questions.questionText: I like ________ sugar in my tea. Do have some, please?
questions.explanation:
The noun 'sugar' is an uncountable noun. The phrase 'a little' is used with uncountable nouns to mean a small, positive quantity.

 The second sentence, 'Do have some, please?' suggests the speaker is offering sugar, which confirms they have a small amount they like and are willing to share.

 'Many' and 'a few' are used with countable nouns. 'Any' is primarily used in questions and negative statements.

questions.questionText: Members of the team sat down under a tree and rested because they were ________ tired after the long journey on foot.
questions.explanation:
The context explains why the team sat down and rested: the journey was long, and they were tired. The word needed is an adverb that intensifies the adjective 'tired.' 

'Extremely' means intensely or very much, which logically explains why they needed rest.

'Hardly' means barely or scarcely, which contradicts the need for rest.

'Quickly' is an adverb of manner, not intensity.

'Fat' is an adjective that does not modify 'tired.'
Therefore, 'extremely' is the correct choice.

questions.questionText: The country was able to register a significant economic growth ________ the negative impacts of both internal and external factors.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires a contrast connector to link the main clause ('significant economic growth') with the following noun phrase ('the negative impacts...'). 

'Despite' and 'in spite of' are followed by a noun or noun phrase. 'In spite' is grammatically incomplete without 'of'.

'Although' and 'even though' are followed by a clause (subject + verb).

Therefore, 'despite' is the only grammatically correct and appropriate choice among the given options.

questions.questionText: I hate going out for a walk ________ the rainy season.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'the rainy season' is a period of time, not a specific point in time. 

The preposition 'during' is used to indicate that something happens within a period of time.

 'While' is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb).

questions.questionText: Our housemaid is really a nice woman. She ________ a mother.
questions.explanation:
The sentence is comparing the housemaid's kindness to that of a mother.

 The phrase 'is like' is used to express similarity or comparison in a non-literal sense, suggesting she has the positive qualities of a mother (caring, loving, etc.).

 'Is as' is incomplete; it would need 'as... as' for comparison (e.g., 'as nice as'). 

'Acts' or 'looks' alone do not convey the intended comparison of character.

questions.questionText: Many more books ________ for the school library next year.
questions.explanation:
The subject is 'Many more books' (an object), and the phrase 'next year' indicates the future. 

Books do not buy themselves; they must be bought by someone (passive action).

 Therefore, the sentence must be in the Future Passive Tense, which is formed with 'will be' + past participle.
 The correct form is 'will be bought'.

questions.questionText: All the participants of the meeting ________ to express their opinions freely.
questions.explanation:
The subject is 'All the participants' (plural), and the sentence describes an action done to them (they were given permission), meaning it must be in the Passive Voice. 

Since the action is an agreement or permission granted in the past or a general state, the Past Passive Tense 'were allowed' (plural form of 'to be' + past participle) is the correct choice.

 'Allowed' (A) is the simple past but needs a form of 'to be' for the passive. 'Allow' (D) is present tense.

questions.questionText: I think they ________ the issue at the next meeting.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'I think' introduces a prediction or an expectation about a future event ('at the next meeting').

 The Future Simple (going to), which is 'are going to discuss,' is used here to express a planned or intended action that is expected to happen. 

'Will be going to discuss' (B) is grammatically incorrect, and (C) and (D) are incomplete forms.

questions.questionText: Although the doctor has warned him several times, he hasn't stopped ________ yet.
questions.explanation:
The verb 'stop' followed by a gerund (verb + -ing) means to cease or quit an ongoing activity.

 The warning is clearly about quitting the habit of consuming alcohol.
 Therefore, 'drinking' is the correct form. 'Stop to drink' would mean the person interrupted their current activity to have a drink.

questions.questionText: If he ________ more carefully, he wouldn't have had the accident.
questions.explanation:
This is a Third Conditional sentence, which expresses an unreal condition in the past and its unreal result in the past.

 The main clause ('he wouldn't have had the accident') uses the structure 'wouldn't have + past participle'. 

The 'if' clause must use the Past Perfect Tense (had + past participle). Therefore, 'had driven' is the correct form.

questions.questionText: The place is a long way from here. I think we ________ take a taxi.
questions.explanation:
The speaker is giving a recommendation or advice for the future action ('take a taxi') based on the present situation ('long way from here').

 The modal verb 'should' is used to express advice or what is advisable. 
Although 'ought to' is a very close synonym, the option is 'ought' without 'to', making 'should' the clearest and most direct answer for expressing advice.

questions.questionText: The new park is really ________. You should go and see it.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires an adjective to describe the park's characteristic, which is that it causes interest or attraction.

 The present participle form 'fascinating' (adjective ending in -ing) is used to describe the quality of a thing that causes a feeling.

 The past participle 'fascinated' (adjective ending in -ed) describes the feeling of a person (e.g., 'I am fascinated').

questions.questionText: We remained idle yesterday we ________ played football ________ watched television.
questions.explanation:
The first part of the sentence, 'We remained idle,' means they did nothing. 

The correlative conjunctions must reflect this negative idea.
 'Neither...nor' is used to mean 'not one and not the other,' fitting the context that they did not play football and they did not watch television.

 'Both...and' and 'either...or' suggest they did at least one or both activities.

questions.questionText: Many people do not ________ it is easy to find jobs these days.
questions.explanation:
The sentence expresses an opinion or belief regarding the ease of finding jobs.

 The verb 'think' means to believe, judge, or consider, and is the only verb among the options that correctly fits the context of expressing a personal belief or judgment.

questions.questionText: My mobile phone is missing. I ________ dropped it somewhere.
questions.explanation:
The first statement establishes a present problem ('missing phone').

 The second sentence offers a possible explanation for a past action. 

The modal verb 'might have' is used to express a possibility in the past (it is possible that I dropped it). 'Couldn't have' expresses impossibility, which contradicts the fact that the phone is missing.

questions.questionText: If you practice regularly, there is no doubt that your English ________ much better.
questions.explanation:
This is a First Conditional sentence, which deals with a real and possible situation in the future.

 The 'if' clause uses the Present Simple ('If you practice regularly'), and the main clause must use the Future Simple Tense to express the likely result. The correct form is 'will be'.

questions.questionText: Next time you come to class don't forget ________ your textbook.
questions.explanation:
The verb 'forget' is followed by an infinitive (to + verb) when referring to a task or action that needs to be done in the future. 

'Don't forget to bring' means 'remember to perform the action of bringing.
' 'Forgetting bringing' (gerund) refers to forgetting that an action already occurred.

questions.questionText: There is a lot of dissatisfaction at present, but ________ that things will improve in the coming years.
questions.explanation:
The sentence uses the contrasting conjunction 'but'.

 The first clause ('a lot of dissatisfaction') suggests a negative situation. 
The second clause ('things will improve in the coming years') suggests a positive outlook.

 The contrast requires a confident statement, which is provided by 'I'm certain' (meaning 'I am sure').

 'I'm not sure' or 'I'm worried' would not create a strong contrast with 'but' followed by a positive prediction.

questions.questionText:
Girum: Let's go to the theatre this afternoon. There is a new play at the National Theatre.

Mihiret: I wish I ________ the time. I have a lot of work today.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'I wish' is used to express regret or a desire for a situation to be different from the current reality. 

To talk about a wish for the present, the structure requires the Past Simple Tense after 'wish,' even though the meaning is present.

 Since Mihiret does not have the time now ('I have a lot of work today'), she says 'I wish I had the time' (Past Simple of 'to have').

questions.questionText: You have ________ to do at home this afternoon, so you can't go out.
questions.explanation:
The sentence implies that there is work to be done, which prevents going out.

 \"Something\" correctly indicates that there is some task to do. 

\"Nothing\" would contradict the reason, \"anything\" is incorrect in this affirmative structure, and \"not\" does not fit grammatically.

questions.questionText: Have all the committee members arrived? ________ the meeting.
options: It is not possible to conduct
It is about time we started
It is the chairman who called
questions.explanation:
The question asks if all members have arrived. If they haven't, the logical consequence or comment is that the meeting cannot proceed. 

The most direct and logical answer that addresses the requirement for the meeting to begin (all members being present) is 'It is not possible to conduct the meeting' (Option B). 

The other options are either grammatically incorrect responses to the setup or irrelevant to the issue of attendance.

questions.questionText: My younger brother is very much interested ________ studying robotics.
questions.explanation:
The correct preposition to follow the adjective 'interested' is 'in'.

 The phrase 'interested in' means having or showing curiosity or concern about something.

 It is followed by a noun or a gerund (like 'studying').

questions.questionText: Muktar went to Jimma ________ see his old friends.
questions.explanation:
The phrase introduces the purpose or reason for the action ('went to Jimma').

 The expression 'in order to' is used to show the purpose of an action and is followed by the base form of the verb ('see'). 

While 'to' alone also expresses purpose, 'in order to' is a complete option that correctly fulfills the function. 'For' expresses purpose but is followed by a noun or gerund (e.g., 'for seeing').

questions.questionText: I wish I ________ a pilot so that I can travel to different parts of the world.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'I wish' expresses a desire for a current reality to be different. 

When wishing for a different state of being in the present, we use the Past Subjunctive (simple past tense), which is conventionally 'were' for all subjects of the verb 'to be' (though 'was' is sometimes used informally).

 Here, 'were' correctly expresses the unreal or contrary-to-fact condition: 'I wish I were a pilot' (but I am not).

questions.questionText: If you don't want to be broke, you ________ your money wisely.
questions.explanation:
The sentence offers advice or a recommendation about a necessary present or future action.

 The modal verb 'ought' (meaning 'should') is used for this purpose and is followed by the infinitive with 'to'.

 Therefore, 'ought to use' is the correct structure. 'Ought to do' (A) is too general, and 'ought have used' (D) is grammatically incorrect (it should be 'ought to have used' for the past).

questions.questionText: Students who came late this morning ________ to report to the Unit Leader's office.
questions.explanation:
The subject is 'Students', who are not performing the action of 'telling,' but are receiving the instruction. This requires the Passive Voice. 

Since the action happened in the past ('came late this morning'), the Past Passive Tense is needed, which is formed with 'were' + past participle ('told'). 'Were told' means 'someone told them'.

questions.questionText: The girl is ________ to take care of herself.
questions.explanation:
The structure 'adjective + enough' is used to indicate that the required quantity or degree of a quality is present.

 The ability to 'take care of herself' is the degree, and 'old' is the required quality. 

Therefore, 'old enough' is the correct word order. 'Enough old' is grammatically incorrect.

questions.questionText: They are working very hard on the project, and ________ they will complete it in time.
questions.explanation:
The first clause ('They are working very hard') gives a reason for a confident prediction in the second clause ('they will complete it in time'). 

The phrase 'I am sure that' is the only option that correctly forms a complete main clause and expresses the necessary certainty or confidence to connect the two ideas logically with the conjunction 'and.'

questions.questionText: My friend says that she ________ all her assignments already.
questions.explanation:
The key word is 'already,' which indicates an action that was completed at some indefinite time in the past but has relevance to the present (the assignments are finished now).

 This requires the Present Perfect Tense, which is formed with 'has/have' + past participle. Therefore, 'has done' is the correct choice.

questions.questionText:

You must do read the test notes to your.

Read notes must to your do the test you.
questions.explanation: The correct word order for the sentence is: 'You must read your notes to do the test.'

questions.questionText: they/home/are/today/early/coming
options: Coming are they early today home?
Are coming early home early they?
Are they coming home early today?
They are coming early home today?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the subject, verb, and object:
- Subject: they
- Verb: are coming
- Object/place: home
- Time/adverb: early today

Step 2: Arrange in correct English order:

Question form: Are + subject + verb + object + time/adverb?

Step 3: Correct sentence: 'Are they coming home early today?'

Therefore, the correct option is C.

questions.questionText:
SECTION Four: Identifying the topic sentence of a paragraph

DIRECTIONS: For items 88 and 89, choose the correct topic sentence of the paragraph given

There are several reasons why my father is in excellent health condition. First, he is very healthy because he has stopped smoking cigarettes. He quit smoking because whenever he climbed stairs, he would stop several times on his way and cough loudly. He also has good health as a result of stopping eating the wrong kinds of food. Third, he is in good physical shape for he does a lot of exercise. He swims three times a week at the local gym. In short, my father is in a better shape than some of his children.
Which of the following sentences best serves as the topic sentence for the paragraph?
options: In short, my father is in a better shape than some of his children.
First, he is very healthy because he has stopped smoking cigarettes.
There are several reasons why my father is in excellent health condition.
He quit smoking because whenever he climbed stairs, he would stop several times on his way and cough loudly.
questions.explanation:
The topic sentence introduces the main idea of the paragraph. 

Here, it presents the general statement about the father's excellent health before the supporting details.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about electric cars and climate change?
options: Electric cars are the future in the automobile industry.
As climate change gets worse, governments are going to start limiting the number of gasoline cars being produced.
Eventually most gas powered cars will be replaced by electric cars.
The cost of gas will continue to rise, which will make it harder for people to afford to run gas powered cars.
questions.explanation:
A good topic sentence introduces the main idea of the paragraph.

 Option B directly connects electric cars to climate change and sets up the discussion of why governments might act, making it the most suitable topic sentence.

SECTION Five: Letter Writing
DIRECTIONS: Items 88-90 are about letter writing. Read each question carefully and choose the best answer according to the context.

Which of the following is an appropriate opening salutation in an informal letter?

Informal letters are written to friends or family. 

'Dear Sarah' is appropriate for an informal letter, while the other options are formal salutations for professionals or acquaintances.

questions.questionText: The sentence, 'I'm extremely delighted to hear that you are going to join the University next year' is possibly taken from:
options: the body of a formal letter
the end of a a formal letter
the beginning of an informal letter
the closing remarks of an informal letter

The sentence expresses personal feelings and excitement, which is typical in the opening of an informal letter.

 It is not formal or part of a closing remark.

questions.questionText:
Section Six: Paragraph Coherence
DIRECTIONS: When put in the correct order, the sentences in items 93 - 96 make complete and coherent paragraphs. From the alternatives A-D given in each case, choose the letter that shows the correct order of the sentences

A. One problem in relation to city buses is that a bus that should arrive at 7:30 in the morning may not arrive until 8: 00 or later.

B. Unfortunately, many people are often late for work or miss important appointments.

C. Poor public transportation system is a big in our city.

D. Moreover, bus drivers often pass up groups of people waiting for the bust at the bus stops.
questions.explanation: Start with the main idea (C), give a specific example (A), add another supporting detail (D), then state the consequence (B).

questions.questionText:
A. At the beginning, my elder sister used to go to gymnastics lessons and showed me how to do some gymnastics when she practiced at home.

B. Now, I take part in gymnastics practice every Saturday.

C. Thus, gymnastics is very special to me, especially because it is something I share with my sister.

D. I started gymnastics when I was six years old and it has been my favourite hobby since then.
questions.explanation: Start with when the writer began gymnastics (D), explain how the sister helped (A), mention current practice (B), and conclude with why it is special (C).

questions.questionText:
A. Similarly, smoking is linked to other lung diseases such as bronchitis.

B. The link between smoking and cancer is well known.

C. Furthermore, there is substantial research evidence that even passive smoking can have long term effects on health.

D. In addition to lung diseases, smokers have a greater risk of heart disease later in life.
questions.explanation: The paragraph order starts with one reason (B: lower cost of living), another reason (D: less crime), then a general topic sentence (C), and finally another example (A: better jobs).

questions.questionText:
A. Some people move to find better jobs.

B. Others want to move to a place with a lower cost of living.

C. There are many reasons why people go to other places to live.

D. Still others want to move to a place with less crime.
questions.explanation: Start with the topic sentence (C) introducing the idea, then give examples: moving for jobs (A), lower cost of living (B), and less crime (D).
